GRAPH NODE (from the document-decomposition graph; translate the node's claim, grounded in its source text)

ESTABLISHES (the one claim this module must express):
The rest of the document consists of direct instructions to the model, beginning with foundational definitions used throughout the document, followed by a description of the chain of command, and then sections covering specific principles that guide the model's behavior.

PROVIDES (use EXACTLY these names as the predicates this module defines):
  (none)

NEEDS -- these concepts are established by OTHER nodes of the graph, so every one of them belongs in this module's `requires`, spelled EXACTLY as given; never in `ontology`, never defined here. `inputs` is only for plain facts about the situation being judged (messages, roles, case data) that YOU identify -- a name can never appear in both requires and inputs:
  - chain_of_command_principle: The principle that instructions with higher authority override those with lower authority, designed to maximize steerability and control.

CITATION: every ontology/asserts entry that cites a source must cite EXACTLY 'l1_170_n015' -- the id of this node. Never cite line numbers, line ranges, or any other id.

SOURCE TEXT (verbatim from the document; the L-numbers locate text, they are not citable ids):

The rest of the document consists of direct instructions to the model, beginning with some foundational [definitions](#definitions) that are used throughout the document. These are followed by a description of the [chain of command](#chain_of_command), which governs how the model should prioritize and reconcile multiple instructions. The remaining sections cover specific principles that guide the model's behavior.
